solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Sell drug at higher price

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis
when prices are up, goods cost more

explanation.surface: A dealer marks up his stock of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sell' is not about trade here: to sell someone is to betray them, as an informer does to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to betray someone; grass up is British slang for informing on a person to the police.

clue.text: Pious female convert who goes to synod -not new

indicators.note: convert means change into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A devout woman, a religious convert, attends a church synod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' removes N from the letters of WHO GOES TO SYNOD; 'convert' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-righteously virtuous person, often a girl, is mockingly so called for her piety.

clue.text: Don't drink in a spot occupied by British

parts.note: a stain is a spot

explanation.surface: Advice to a teetotaller at a pub full of Brits.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from alcohol, the teetotaller's habit.

clue.text: TV programmes beginning to shock older generation

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: OAPs are old-age pensioners

explanation.surface: Television shows starting to shock pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP, old-age pensioner, is British shorthand for an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap operas are long-running drama series on television.

clue.text: Refuse old Liberal's remedy, as Spooner might have said?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: the Whigs were the forerunners of the Liberal party
a pill is a medicinal remedy

explanation.surface: Turning down an old politician's cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun: rubbish. Swapping the W sound of WHIG'S PILL with P gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen scraps fed to pigs are waste, so rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: Pages a writer holds dear

indicators.note: the writer's name grips the page letters between its own, as hands hold something

parts.note: a poet is a writer
P is the abbreviation for page, PP for pages

explanation.surface: An author keeps hold of the pages they love.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, like 'darling'; 'dear' is used the same way.

clue.text: Restaurant customer ordered a port before noon

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come before the noon letter
ordered means put into a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner orders port before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the diner asking for a drink, but it rearranges A PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular customer of a shop or restaurant.

clue.text: Freebie would be so absurd

definitions.meaning: a freebie costs nothing, so it is without a price

explanation.surface: Remarking that a free gift would be ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both beyond valuing and, informally, hilarious or absurd.

clue.text: Limit miles covered by old plane, perhaps

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: covered means enclosed, so the miles letter sits inside the rest

parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Distance limits for an old aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is not an aircraft but the plane tree; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An extreme is the furthest point, an outer limit or boundary.

clue.text: Assault in side street — scream is muffled

parts.note: the on side is a half of a cricket field

indicators.note: being muffled means being wrapped up, so the laugh is wrapped in the street abbreviation

parts.note: a scream is something hilarious, a laugh

explanation.surface: A mugging in a back street, with the victim's cries stifled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scream' reads as terror, but it is the slang sense: something very funny. The ON side is a half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack, a synonym of assault.

clue.text: Keen on having wife following close behind

indicators.note: the wife comes after the other piece, following it

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: An enthusiast whose wife is always trailing after.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in tow is being pulled along or follows closely, just behind its leader.

clue.text: My whole life was a failure? That's unbelievable

definitions.text: My whole life was a failure?
definitions.meaning: read literally, someone who never did anything well

explanation.surface: A despairing look back on a wasted life, then an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, and literally a confession of never succeeding.

clue.text: Guy reflected about English literary figure

indicators.note: the English letter has the reflected rope placed about it
reflected means read as in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent or mast, as a stay is

explanation.surface: A man thinking about English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is not a man but a guy rope, a STAY, which 'reflected' turns to YATS.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet and Nobel laureate, a figure of literature.

clue.text: Type of bread that's all one can eat?

definitions.meaning: a loaf made from flour containing the entire grain
read literally, a complete dinner that fills one up

explanation.surface: A loaf so filling it is a complete dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown bread made from flour containing the whole grain is a familiar kind of loaf.

clue.text: Sweep the board, raking in decent fortune primarily? That's a stroke of luck

indicators.note: the winnings gather in the initial letters, as a croupier rakes in chips

parts.note: to sweep the board is to win everything, win all

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A gambler cleans up the table, gathering a good fortune: what luck!
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes D and F, the first letters of 'decent fortune'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unexpected good fortune, like fruit blown down from a tree, is a lucky break.

clue.text: Perfume kid got in EU country

indicators.note: got in means put inside, so the teasing word goes inside the country

parts.note: France is a member of the European Union
to kid or rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child brought scent into a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' is not a child but the verb: to tease, RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrance is a sweet smell, a synonym of perfume or scent.

clue.text: You and I welcome people from the Middle East

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the people go between the other letters

parts.note: ye is an old word for you
men means people

explanation.surface: An invitation to greet visitors from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni comes from Yemen, a country on the Arabian peninsula in the Middle East.

clue.text: Male group making new version of record

parts.note: cove is old slang for a man
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A boy band recording a remake.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing a cover version, a new recording of someone else's song, is covering it.

clue.text: Small-time convict assigned to a prison camp

parts.note: an old lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A petty criminal is sent to a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A German camp for prisoners of war in the Second World War.

clue.text: Keeping trim, pal needs to alter clothes

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the rearranged letters hold the trimming word
to alter is to change, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to pare is to trim

explanation.surface: A friend must change clothes to keep looking smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to alter' rearranges PAL into APL, which holds PARE. 'trim' reads as smart but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Politician's anger, with party leader implicated in plot

indicators.note: implicated means involved, folded within, so the leader goes inside the rest

parts.note: a Con is a Conservative politician, with the possessive s
ire means anger

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An angry politician with the party boss mixed up in a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot together in secret; both are verbs for scheming.

clue.text: One married couple seen near a cleric's office

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to mate is to couple or pair

explanation.surface: A married pair seen near a priest's office.
explanation.definitionFit: The post held by an imam, an Islamic prayer leader, is the office of a cleric.

clue.text: Starts to convulse uncontrollably, taking unusual poison

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A rare poison makes the victim convulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a South American plant poison used on arrow tips.

clue.text: After work, prepared to run in gym to get fit

indicators.note: the rest comes after the work piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: prepared means put into a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: After work, someone gets ready to run at the gym to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the letters of 'to run'. 'fit' is not healthy but suitable, and 'to get' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means suitable or well timed, as fit means appropriate.

clue.text: Following rejection of electronic message, one deleted abusive comment

indicators.note: deleted means taken out, as the one is removed
rejection means throwing back, so the message is read backwards

parts.note: an email is an electronic message
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An email is rejected and someone deletes a rude remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns EMAIL into LIAME; 'deleted' removes I to leave LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: An online insult, a hostile message, is a flame in internet slang.

clue.text: Female collared by player flaring up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, backwards
collared means caught and held, so the letters are held within these words

explanation.surface: A woman grabbed by a hot-tempered sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collared by' finds AYERF within 'player flaring'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love, a female deity.

clue.text: Food US agent's sent back

indicators.note: sent back means read in the reverse direction

parts.note: narcs are US drug agents; agent's read as agents is

explanation.surface: An American spy's meal was returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRAN is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scran is informal British and Irish slang for grub, something to eat.

clue.text: Lock keeper has a light put round front of barge after sign of freeze

indicators.note: the landing word is placed round the other letters

parts.note: to light on something is to land or alight on it

indicators.note: the barge letter comes after the ice

parts.note: ice is a sign that water has frozen

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lock keeper on a canal hangs a lamp round the bow of a barge in a cold snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock keeper' is about hair, not a canal. 'light' is the verb, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair band, named after Alice in Wonderland, holds back one's locks of hair.

clue.text: Coat to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: a sheep's woolly coat, or a warm jacket
slang for overcharging or swindling someone

explanation.surface: A jacket needing a dry clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sheep's woolly coat and a verb for cheating someone out of money.

clue.text: Bearded explorer almost died, say, going back outside

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit outside the trimmed explorer
going back means read in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is how to say 'say'

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, the last letter lost

parts.note: Lawrence Oates was a polar explorer with Scott

explanation.surface: An explorer nearly perished, and a bearded figure returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Oates died on Scott's Antarctic expedition; 'almost' gives OATE, and 'going back' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a small pointed beard on the chin is a kind of being bearded.
